title: Navimower 0.3.4 — multi-mower support and mapped mower settings

## Highlights

Navimower 0.3.4 promotes the tested 0.3.4 beta line to a normal release. It combines the multi-mower work, telemetry and history hardening, safer settings writes, and the newly mapped Navimow app controls.

## Multiple mowers and cloud identity

- Each mower can be configured as its own Home Assistant config entry with its own entities, map, history and MQTT connection.
- Private-cloud identity is deterministic for the same account, avoiding duplicate device identities during reloads.
- The setup flow always shows the mower selector so shared and multi-mower accounts can select the intended robot.
- A separate dedicated private-cloud account per parallel config entry remains the recommended arrangement.

## Telemetry, map and history reliability

- Battery, task progress, active-zone progress, coverage, mowed area and map area use freshness-aware source selection and last-known-good retention.
- Official MQTT and private-cloud values keep their separate meanings instead of being treated as interchangeable counters.
- Map data avoids unnecessary deep-copy work during normal state updates.
- Provisional empty history sessions and immediate startup/reset stubs are filtered so they do not consume history slots.
- Map Edit states are reported without falsely marking the mower as docked.

## Safer setting writes

Mower settings now use one robot-first/cloud-second transaction. Home Assistant does not refresh from the eventually consistent cloud between those writes. Acknowledged values are kept in the local write-through cache, followed by delayed authoritative cloud confirmation.

The release includes the verified mower-side hexadecimal encoding fixes for:

- Geo-fence radius;
- Snow delay;
- Frost cutoff time;
- Maximum mowing temperature.

Snow delay is displayed as a simple 1–7 day slider while the mower and cloud continue to use the underlying hour count.

## Mapped controls

Depending on the mower model, firmware and returned `set_list`, Home Assistant can expose:

- Work mode: Standard, Efficient and Precision;
- Geo-fence alarm and radius;
- Rain, rain sensor, weather forecast and delay-after-rain controls;
- Weather sensitivity, frost, snow, strong-wind and high-temperature controls;
- Do not disturb with separate 15-minute start and end selects;
- Energy saver;
- Night mowing;
- Animal-friendly mode and Night light;
- H215 Terrain adapt, Edge sense and Edge sense mode.

Night mowing uses the confirmed legacy write format and reads the nested camera-box setting used by the app.

## Model-specific brightness

The two tested mower families use different fields even though both fields may appear in their raw settings:

- **H215 — Night light brightness:** Default, Dim and Extra dim through `lightIntensity`.
- **X390 — Brightness:** Dim and Extra dim through `nightLightLevel`.

The model gate prevents the inactive duplicate control from being created.

## Supported entities only

Setting switches, selects and numbers are created only when the current model and a successful private-cloud `set_list` response support them. Supported setting entities are enabled by default. Stale unsupported setting entities left by an earlier beta are removed only after a valid `set_list` read, never because of a temporary cloud failure.

## Testing scope

Primary development and live bidirectional setting tests were performed on an **H215** in the European/FRA region. An **X390** was used for secondary multi-mower, map, telemetry and model-specific settings validation. Other models, firmware versions, accounts and regions may expose different fields; unsupported settings are therefore presence-gated and should be reported with sanitized diagnostics.

Navimower still uses an undocumented private-cloud protocol and is not affiliated with or supported by Segway, Ninebot, Navimow or Willand. Keep a Home Assistant backup and verify mower commands in a safe environment.
